page: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by 16 AWS Inferentia chips offering a collective total of 128 GB of accelerator memory. The instance includes 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while containing no bundled local storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities alongside notable limitations in specific generative workloads. In CPU testing, the system demonstrated strong performance in PassMark CPU tests, Clang compilation, and multi-core stress-ng tests. Memory operations showed substantial bandwidth, exceeding 232 GB/sec in large-block read operations and reaching 79.6 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-core execution metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier. In large language model evaluations, prompt ingestion processing performs at an average level, but text generation rates for both small and medium models scored in the lowest percentile tier, highlighting the architectural focus of first-generation Inferentia silicon on non-autoregressive or bounded inference tasks rather than high-speed continuous text generation.

From an infrastructure and cost-efficiency perspective, the inf1.24xlarge consolidates high network throughput and dedicated inference hardware into a dense deployment. The absence of local disk requires reliant attachments to network-based storage volumes, which introduces external I/O considerations. This configuration is best targeted at machine learning inference pipelines optimized for AWS Neuron SDK, computer vision processing, natural language comprehension, and high-concurrency microservice architectures requiring dense accelerator clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for deep learning inference workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance integrates 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon 8275CL cores at 2.5 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 system memory and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Machine learning acceleration is delivered via 16 dedicated AWS Inferentia chips with 128 GB of combined accelerator memory. In benchmark testing, the platform shows strong results in multi-core compute, system memory bandwidth, and high-volume Redis operations, while single-thread speed ranks in the mid-range. While autoregressive LLM text generation rates fall within lower percentiles, prompt processing and multi-threaded throughput remain capable. With no bundled local storage, persistent I/O relies on network-attached storage. The instance is suited for batch machine learning inference, computer vision models, and large-scale analytical inference pipelines.
